    Estimate an epidemiological delay distribution

    Source: R/outbreak-delays.R
    epi_delay_dist.Rd

    Fits lognormal, gamma and Weibull distributions to delays between two events, such as symptom onset to reporting, onset to death or the serial interval, by maximum likelihood. With daily data both events are known only to the day, so the observed delay is doubly interval censored; with an ongoing outbreak, long delays are not yet observed, so the data are right truncated. Ignoring either biases the estimated mean, usually downwards (Park et al. 2024). This function accounts for both, using the exact (closed-form) probability of each whole-day delay when the primary event is uniformly distributed within its day (Charniga et al. 2024).

    Usage

    epi_delay_dist(
  .data,
  delay,
  max_delay = NULL,
  family = c("lognormal", "gamma", "weibull"),
  censoring = c("double", "none"),
  conf_level = 0.95
)

    Arguments

    .data

    A data frame with one row per individual.

    delay

    Observed delays. With censoring = "double", whole numbers of days (0 or more); with censoring = "none", exact positive delays.

    max_delay

    Optional column with the longest delay that could have been observed for each individual (days from the primary event to the end of data collection). Supplying it corrects for right truncation.

    family

    One or more of "lognormal", "gamma" and "weibull".

    censoring

    "double" (default) for whole-day data, "none" for exact delays.

    conf_level

    Confidence level for the mean (delta method on the log scale).

    Value

    A tep_delay tibble with one row per family, best first by AIC: family, parameters (a list column of named estimates), mean, mean_lower, mean_upper, sd, median, q95 (95th percentile), loglik, aic, delta_aic, n, censoring and truncated. Pass it to epi_delay_pmf() for discretised probabilities to use with epi_cfr(), epi_nowcast() or epi_rt().

    References

    Park, S. W., Akhmetzhanov, A. R., Charniga, K., Cori, A., Davies, N. G., Dushoff, J., Funk, S., Gostic, K., Grenfell, B., Linton, N. M., Lipsitch, M., Lison, A., Overton, C. E., Ward, T. and Abbott, S. (2024). Estimating epidemiological delay distributions for infectious diseases. medRxiv. doi:10.1101/2024.01.12.24301247

    Charniga, K., Park, S. W., Akhmetzhanov, A. R., Cori, A., Dushoff, J., Funk, S., Gostic, K. M., Linton, N. M., Lison, A., Overton, C. E., Pulliam, J. R. C., Ward, T., Cauchemez, S. and Abbott, S. (2024). Best practices for estimating and reporting epidemiological delay distributions of infectious diseases. PLOS Computational Biology, 20, e1012520. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1012520

    Examples

    set.seed(1)
onset <- runif(300, 0, 40)
report <- onset + rlnorm(300, 1.5, 0.5)
d <- data.frame(delay = floor(report) - floor(onset))
epi_delay_dist(d, delay)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 14
#>   family  parameters  mean mean_lower mean_upper    sd median   q95 loglik   aic
#>   <chr>   <list>     <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 lognor… <dbl [2]>   5.12       4.81       5.44  2.79   4.49 10.4   -685. 1374.
#> 2 gamma   <dbl [2]>   5.10       4.81       5.40  2.55   4.68  9.88  -686. 1375.
#> 3 weibull <dbl [2]>   5.11       4.81       5.42  2.63   4.81  9.88  -696. 1396.
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: delta_aic <dbl>, n <int>, censoring <chr>,
#> #   truncated <lgl>

# Only reports up to day 40 are known: correct for right truncation
d$max_delay <- 40 - floor(onset)
seen <- d[d$delay <= d$max_delay, ]
epi_delay_dist(seen, delay, max_delay = max_delay, family = "lognormal")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 14
#>   family  parameters  mean mean_lower mean_upper    sd median   q95 loglik   aic
#>   <chr>   <list>     <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 lognor… <dbl [2]>   5.14       4.79       5.52  2.80   4.51  10.4  -598. 1199.
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: delta_aic <dbl>, n <int>, censoring <chr>,
#> #   truncated <lgl>
